rows.en:
You see it?
It's just an ordinary clock, nothing special about it.
It's pretty dusty, though.
Let's open it up.{p}

...There's no battery in it anymore.
That's why it doesn't run.
But you know, this clock is strange.
Say you move the hands, right?
Before you know it, they've gone back to 10:20.{p}

"Whoa!"
The other five all screamed at once.
They looked, and on the wall where the clock had hung, there was a stain like a human face.
For an instant, it looked like a skull.
...But when they looked closely, it was just a stain.{p}

"A skull-shaped stain★"
{f:I|I} hurriedly cut in.
A stain that looked like a skull{f:, he said|...}?
Wasn't that the same thing I'd seen in the restroom earlier{f:|}?
Was he telling me that same stain was behind that clock{f:|}?
Somehow, I had a bad feeling about this.
Unable to put it into words, I said nothing, and Hosoda gave {f:me|me} a puzzled look.
And then the story went on.{p}

...Why not?
I just know you and I would get along great.
Come on, be my friend.{p}You will, won't you? Please?
I don't want to be your friend
Oh well, I'll be your friend

That's cruel.
Do you really enjoy hurting me that much?
Were you always such a mean person?
Hosoda looked at {f:me|me} reproachfully.
...Oh well, I guess there's no helping it{f:|}.
{f:I|I} nodded.
"{f:Sorry|I'm sorry}. {f:Fine, I'll be your friend|Let's be friends}."{p}

Okay, got it.
Then I'll tell you.
After all, it's a request from you, my friend.
...The three of them headed off together to the faculty room.
You go straight down the hallway, turn the corner, and the faculty room is right there.
It's not a long way at all.
They still looked fairly relaxed.
But when they turned the corner, there was no faculty room.
In front of them, the very hallway they should have just walked down stretched on and on.
When they looked back, there was the classroom door.
They hadn't moved a single step.
But how could that be?
Just to be sure, they started walking again.
They walked to the end of the hallway and turned the corner.
...Sure enough, a long hallway stretched on in front of them.{p}

And behind them, the classroom door.
That settled it.
They were trapped.
Who had trapped them, they didn't know.
How, they didn't know either.
All they knew was that space had twisted around into something like a Mobius strip.
You know, that loop you make from a ribbon with one twist in it, where if you trace it with your finger, you can't tell the back from the front anymore.
"I can't take this anymore☆"
The girl who'd burst into tears earlier screamed.
But this time, the other girl didn't comfort her.
I guess she was in no state to.
She was shaking like a leaf.
As the only guy left, he must have felt it was all on him.{p}{a}{f:, what would you do|, what would you do in his place}?
Search the classroom
Search the hallway

First, naturally, they checked the windows.
It had been a muggy day, so the windows were left open to let in even a little breeze.
But at some point, they'd been closed.
Without a word, the three of them tried to open them.
Because once you start wondering who closed them... you just keep imagining scarier and scarier things.
But the windows wouldn't open.
It was like they'd rusted shut.
Ridiculous, right?
Those windows had been open just a moment ago.
After a few tries, someone must have hit their limit.
"I'm going home! I'm going home, I said☆"
The one shrieking wasn't the girl who'd been crying, but the one who'd been comforting her.{p}

She grabbed her bag and ran out of the classroom.
"Hey, wait!"
He started to go after her, but then the other girl would be left all alone, and he couldn't do that to her.
He stayed put.
And that turned out to be the right choice.
Because a few seconds later...{p}

The two of them went over to the door and saw something crawling in the hallway, where the lights had gone out.
What was it?
As they strained their eyes, it inched a little closer.
It was the girl who had run off.
Still lying face down, she was desperately lifting her head and reaching out her hand.{p}

"Help... me..."
A hoarse voice begged for help.{p}
And then something big was flung down at the two of them, landing at their feet.{p}
They jumped out of the way, and saw that it was an arm, still tightly clutching a school bag.{p}

"Eeeeeeeek☆"
The girl screamed.
At the sound, the darkness in the hallway swelled.
The darkness itself was alive.{p}

The endless darkness spreading outside the windows.
And that darkness surging straight toward them.
The window glass was creaking.
Any second now, the windows would break.
And once that happened, there would be no way left for them to survive.
...In that case.
An idea came to him.{p}What do you think it was?
Sacrifice the girl and escape himself
Sacrifice himself and let the girl escape

He opened the door to the hallway.
The darkness was only a few meters away now.
He swallowed hard and shoved the girl standing next to him.
She had trusted him completely, so she stumbled out into the hallway without a struggle.
The darkness caught her by the legs.
She was dragged to the floor, and she looked up at him.
With eyes full of resentment, as if she couldn't believe it.{p}

As he ran, he spotted an emergency exit.
He was saved!{p}

He took a run at the door and slammed into it.
The door shook, but it wouldn't open.{p}

But there was no time left to try anywhere else.
The darkness could catch up with him at any moment, after all.{p}

He threw his body against the door again and again.
And at last, the door opened.{p}

As he burst through, stumbling, someone caught him.
Relieved that he'd finally reached somewhere safe, he nearly sank to the ground.
But whoever had caught him kept pulling at him, trying to make him stand up.
"No, no, you mustn't rest in a place like this.
You're going this way..."
A voice he knew.{p}

He looked up with a start. It was that girl.
The girl he'd shoved out and fed to the darkness.
Between her lashes there were no whites and no pupils, only spreading darkness.
He tried to run, but she held him tight and wouldn't let go.
The corners of her mouth curled into a small smile.
"Let's go... together..."
He froze, and the next instant, the darkness wrapped around him.{p}

"...And that's how it went.
The next day, the teachers searched for the six of them.
But not a single one was ever found.
As if they'd melted away."
Hosoda finished his story.
It seemed to have gotten a little darker than before{f:|}.{p}

{f:I|I} found myself looking around.
I didn't want to stay here much longer{f:|}.
"Thank you very much.
Well then, shall we head back to the club room?"
As {f:I|I} tried to wrap things up, Hosoda cut me off.{p}

"Hold on.
The story isn't over yet.
Why do you think we went to the trouble of coming all the way here?"
"How would I know?
It's late, so maybe we should call it a day..."
"The darkness here, you see, is still alive."
Hosoda whispered, out of nowhere.
"It's alive, and it still wants food... Look."
He pointed at a corner of the classroom.{p}

Maybe it was my imagination, but the darkness seemed to squirm on the old floorboards.
My mouth went dry in an instant.
No way... it had to be my imagination{f:|, right}.
I only thought I saw something{f:|}.{p}

...Hosoda was smiling from ear to ear.
"You don't want to believe it, huh?
I can't blame you, but think about how I'd know a story like this."
Clowning around, he rolled both his eyes.{p}

Then his eyeballs bulged out.
More than halfway out of their lids.
Looking closely, they weren't real eyeballs.
They were cloudy, round, opaque glass... just like marbles.{p}

With a hard clack, clack, the two marbles dropped to the floor and rolled away.
And from behind them, an infinite darkness peered out, stretching on forever.
"It's very spacious inside the darkness.
If I don't bring in more of our kind, I get so lonely I can't stand it..."
Hosoda, with eyes of darkness, came closer.
Would {f:I|I}, too, stare into the darkness and wander around like this, looking for more of my kind{f:|}...?
As the darkness swallowed me from my hands and feet inward, {f:I|I} kept dazedly thinking about that.{p}

He turned to face the girl.
"I'm going to clear us a path somehow.
While I do, you get away."
"But what about you?"
"Once you're out, I'll be right behind you."
That's what he said, but he didn't really believe he'd get away too.
I guess he thought, if only the girl could make it...
{f:If it were me|I'm sure}, {f:I could never think like that|those two were good friends, just like us}.
He opened the door to the hallway.{p}
The darkness was only a few meters away now.{p}
He swallowed hard and flung his own bag out there.{p}

With a squelching crunch, the darkness swallowed the bag.
Just how many victims were inside that pitch-black belly?
He shuddered in spite of himself.
But he couldn't stand there like that forever.{p}

He shoved the girl away.
She stumbled off in the direction away from the darkness.
"Run, hurry!"
Shouting that, he raised a chair over his head.
And he hurled himself at the darkness.{p}

The darkness spread wide for an instant and engulfed him.
For a moment, he lost consciousness.
...Maybe it was really a lot longer than that, though.
But when he came to, it didn't feel like that much time had passed.
Yeah, that's right.
The darkness didn't eat him.{p}

And then, what do you know, a monster came running at him from over there.
An ugly body thickly covered in purple scales, and huge, bulging eyes.
Drool was streaming from its mouth, which was split all the way to its ears, and it was screaming words he couldn't make out.
He felt his life was in danger.
Looking around, he saw a bat lying on the ground that the baseball team must have forgotten to put away.{p}
He picked it up and went at the monster, swinging.{p}
Head, shoulders, arms, he didn't care where, he just beat it.{p}

At the same moment, someone grabbed him from behind and pinned his arms.
It was the janitor, with a rigid look.
"What are you doing?!"
What did it look like he was doing?
He'd been taking out this monster.
He was about to say so, and he looked down at the monster's corpse.{p}

But the one lying there was the girl he was supposed to have saved from the darkness. Blood was running from her head, and she lay limp with her eyes shut.
One look told him she wasn't alive anymore.{p}

"I heard a racket and came to see, and here you are beating this girl!
Why on earth would you do this to her★"
The janitor asked him.
There was no way he could answer, right?
What he'd been beating was supposed to be a monster.
But it wasn't, was it?
Which leaves only one possibility.
In his eyes, his friend, the girl, had looked like a monster.
So when she ran over to him because she was worried, he thought she was attacking him.
Instead of eating him, the darkness warped his sight, I think.
Knowing full well what it would lead to.{p}

If so, that's unbelievably cruel, isn't it?
Because his misfortune didn't end there.
What do I mean?
The next day, the teachers searched the building.
And... they found the bodies of the other four, one after another.
The darkness got all of them, I guess.
Apparently they were in a horrible state.
And that got pinned on him too.
Nobody listened to his side of the story.
After all, he'd been caught red-handed.{p}

What happened to him after that?
...Well, I don't know.
I'd guess he got locked up somewhere, like a prison or a juvenile detention center.
The story was over.
{f:I|I} raised my lowered head and looked at Hosoda.{p}

...The one sitting there wasn't Hosoda.
No, it wasn't even human.
Six eyes, like compound eyes, peered out through patchy tufts of hair.
Its crooked, jagged teeth glinted.{p}

"A... a monster★"
{f:I|I} jumped back.
The monster was saying something as it came toward me.
Wasn't there anything{f:|}?
A weapon, anything I could fight it with.
I felt around in my pockets, and my fingertips touched something hard.
A box cutter{f:|}.
The one I'd used for the club, when we were clipping articles for a scrapbook.
{f:I|I} held it ready.
The monster's arm reached for the box cutter.
I won't let you!
{f:|Frantically, }I swung the cutter, and the blade slashed the monster's eye!{p}

Spurting green blood, the monster slowly collapsed.
Breathing hard, {f:I|I} looked around.
I felt like I'd been with someone until just a moment ago.
...Had I?
{f:I|I} {f:was alone from the start, wasn't I?|feel like I was alone from the start.}
{f:That's right|Yes, that's it}.
{f:I|I} {f:am|am} all alone.
I defeated the monster, so the ruler of this world is {f:me|me}.
...Still, I'm tired{f:|}.
{f:I|I} yawned and curled up next to the monster's corpse.
I'll sleep a little.
After all, there's nothing left to threaten {f:me|me}.{p}
Just then, I thought I heard the darkness that had crept up to my feet let out a laugh.{p}

Right, they searched the hallway too.
If they could find the spot where space was warped, they might be able to escape through it.
With their eyes peeled wide, they went along feeling over the walls and floor.
"Oh, look!"
One of the girls pointed at a corner of the hallway.{p}

When they peered through, they could see a green plain on the other side!
They tried scratching around the crack.
Bits crumbled away.
The wall fell apart almost absurdly easily.{p}

And spread out before them was, sure enough, a vast plain.
"We're saved!"
Shouting that, the girls ran out onto the grass.
Then they turned back to him.
"Hurry up, come on!"
But he couldn't take that step.
He'd realized something was wrong.
A grassland stretching as far as the eye could see didn't seem like it could be in Japan, for one thing.{p}

While he hesitated, the wall started to grow.
The part that had crumbled swelled back up all on its own.
Before his eyes, the hole in the wall shrank to about half its size.
He tried scratching at it, but the wall that had been so fragile a moment ago was now as hard as a steel plate.
"Hurry, come over here!"
The girls started to panic.
But all the while, the hole kept closing.{p}

And finally, it was back to being just the crack it had started as.
He'd been left behind alone, on this side of the world.
In warped space, no less.
But in the end, the girls stayed missing too.
They'd made it out, but maybe the other side of the crack was warped space as well.{p}

What did he do after that, you ask?
He's still missing.
And so is everyone else, while we're at it.
Maybe they're all still in here somewhere.{p}

...Just kidding.
Hosoda finished his story.
{f:I|I} couldn't help speaking up.
"Going out of your way to tell a story like that here, of all places.
That's in bad taste."{p}
And I stood up.{p}

When I looked back, an identical long hallway stretched on behind me.
What was going on{f:|}?
Had Hosoda's story come true{f:|}?
But in the story, the classroom door was supposed to be behind them{f:|}.
And yet...
{f:I|I} hurriedly ran back the way I'd come.
No matter how far I ran, the classroom door didn't appear.
This can't be!
When I looked a moment ago, the hallway was only about ten meters long.
Had {f:I|I}, too, wandered into the warped space{f:|}?
I didn't want to admit it.
{f:I|I} kept running.
Maybe someday I'd find the door.
So I ran.
Ran.
Ran.
Ran.
Then I noticed that at some point, a shadow had started running alongside {f:me|me}.
I turned to look.{p}

A half-skeletonized man was running with his teeth bared.
His eyes turned to {f:me|me}.
{f:I|I} knew who he was.
He was the guy from the story just now{f:|}.
He'd kept on running for all those long years, even after dying and turning to bone{f:|}.
His eyes looked somehow happy.
It was only natural, now that he had {f:me|me} as a companion{f:|, I suppose}.{p}He and {f:I|I} would probably keep running forever down that endless hallway.
Through the warped world.{p}

Right.
He decided to start looking with the nearest restroom.{p}

But there was nobody in there.
Instead, big letters had been scrawled across the wall.
In rough handwriting, it said
"Go to the third floor."
Just like that.
The only ones who'd pull something like this were those two.
They really were trying to scare the rest of them.
He got a little angry.
Then he decided to go up to the third floor.{p}

As he climbed the stairs, wouldn't you know it, he heard snickering from somewhere above.
It was them.
He wasn't going to be satisfied until he'd given them a piece of his mind.
He charged up the last few steps in one go.
And he shouted:{p}

"Knock it off☆"
...But there was no reaction.
The feeling that someone was there, which he'd had until then, had vanished without a trace.
Even though he hadn't heard anyone running off.
Only then did he realize he'd come all the way up to the third floor.
Come to think of it, Hanako-san was supposed to haunt the restroom on this floor, wasn't she?
He broke out in goosebumps all over.{p}

On the wall in front of him, a whole crowd of skull crests had surfaced.
He was startled, of course.
But they weren't skulls.
They looked just like them, but they were only stains on the wall.
Apparently they were shaped like human faces, so he'd mistaken them.
"Oh, is that all..."
Just as he let out a sigh.{p}

With a skittering rustle, the stains squirmed.
The skulls sat up, slow and heavy, as if they'd been buried in the wall.{p}

When they reached the stairs, the skulls went rolling up them, see.
He followed them, nervously.
Because he wanted to know where the skulls were headed.
Roll, roll, roll... up the stairs the skulls went.
And before long, they made it all the way to the third floor.{p}

But it seemed the skulls' parade wasn't over yet.
They went rolling off down the hallway.{p}
Just then, he suddenly heard a scream.{p}

At the same moment, the skulls in front of him vanished, just like that.
Had it been a hallucination...?{p}

He tried going up the stairs.
He figured that, on some whim, they might have picked the restroom one floor up.{p}

But the restroom light was off.
It looked like it wasn't the second floor after all.{p}
That left the first floor and the third. What should he do?
Go back to the first floor
Try going up to the third floor

He decided to go back to the first floor.
After all, the restroom closest to the classroom was the best bet, right?{p}

He decided to go up to the third floor.
That meant walking the creaking hallway back to the stairs again.{p}

He didn't open it.
The door opened all by itself.{p}

Standing startlingly close was a woman with a bobbed haircut.
She was wearing a sailor uniform soaked in blood.
Her eyes flashed for an instant inside a white mask.
And then she wrapped him in a tight embrace.
She pressed her head hard against his neck, and he couldn't help arching his back.
That leaves you looking straight up at the ceiling, right?
And so he saw them.{p}

A whole crowd of women, stuck to the ceiling like geckos.
Short-haired ones, ones in braids, all kinds of women in blood-soaked sailor uniforms and white masks, clinging up there.
They were staring down at him.
He opened his throat to scream, and in a flash the woman bit it clean through.
As his blood sprayed up, he was thinking.{p}

Those small black creatures that had been carrying the three of them... maybe they were those skull stains...
Maybe they were bringing food to these women. That's what he thought.{p}

Why say that now, after all this?
We're friends, aren't we?
We stick together, in good times and bad, right?
I already think of you as my best friend.
That's why I want you to solve the mystery of Hanako-san.
Can't you understand how I feel, as your best friend?
So it's okay, isn't it?
Let's go.
Right?
...Will you nod for me?{p}

Right, of course.
You're someone who doesn't want to go to the restroom, aren't you?
...Fine, I get it.
I get it perfectly.
Even after I've set everything up so nicely for you, you still won't go near a restroom.
Actually, I've had my eye on you this whole time.
You're kind of famous in some circles, you know.
Didn't you know that?{p}

I overheard some first-years talking about it.
They said you never, ever go to the restroom.
I thought, no way, that's ridiculous.
But it sounded interesting.
So I've been curious about you ever since.
And it turns out... you really don't go, do you?
I asked your classmates, and they say you don't go even once a day.
That's just not natural, no matter how you look at it.
And even now, when it's for your own project, you come out saying you won't go to the restroom.{p}

...But you know, I've figured it out.
You hate restrooms, don't you?
The smell in there, the air, or maybe the tiles or whatever they're made of. You can't stand them, can you?
That's how I figured it out.
You're not human.
If you were human, you'd always need the restroom.
You couldn't possibly loathe it that much.
So what are you?
An alien, maybe?{p}

"You've disguised yourself very well.
But you can't fool my eyes."
He came closer.
His knife stayed {f:raised|raised}.
"I've tried dogs and cats, but I wonder what an alien's body looks like inside."
{f:What did he just say|What is he saying}?
Is this guy {f:even in his right mind|even sane}?
{f:Me|Me}, an alien?
Just because I don't go to the restroom, he'd been thinking that about me?
To tell the truth, it {f:wasn't as if I never went|isn't as if I never go} at all.
It's just my constitution; I go less often than normal people, that's all...
No, this {f:was|is} no time to argue about that.
What {f:was he going|is he going} to do★
{f:He must have read|Maybe he read} the look on {f:my|my} face.{p}

Hosoda grinned.
"I'm going to dissect you.
Don't worry, it'll be over soon."
His eyes weren't sane.
"S-Somebody!"
A scream burst out of my mouth before I knew it.
"Hel..."{p}
Before I could finish, an arm shot out and {f:I|I} was shoved to the floor.{p}

Hosoda climbed on top of me, straddling me.
"It's okay, it's okay."{p}

I couldn't tell if it was heat or pain.
Through my blurring vision I saw Hosoda, spattered with my green blood, grinning.
"Just as I thought."
{f:I|I} cursed myself.
The mission {f:was a failure|had failed}.
How could I slip up like this...{p}Bitterly regretting that I would die on this faraway alien planet, {f:I|I} slowly closed my eyes.{p}

Hosoda's fingers clamped down hard on my shoulder.
"I won't let you go home."
A smile that gave off something dangerous.
Because his eyes weren't smiling.
Between his narrowed lids, silver-white pupils were glinting.
This isn't Hosoda★
"Who are you...?"
My voice came out hoarse.
"Since when..."
At that, Hosoda(?)'s smile grew wider.
"Who'd have thought you'd stay fooled right to the very end?
It's a little early, but let's finish this here..."{p}

As he said it, the skin of his face came sloughing off with a wet slop.
From beneath gentle Hosoda's face, huge goggling eyeballs emerged.
I remembered seeing something like it in the science room, long ago.
The muscle diagram on the anatomical model.
It looked just like that.
The thing was making a low chuckling sound in its throat.
It was laughing, watching me cower.{p}

From somewhere it produced a white mask like a Noh mask, and pressed it onto its face.
The pure white, uncanny face came close to mine.
"This is me... the one who dwells in the old school building."
It whispered in my ear.
"I caught this one as he was leaving the classroom and took his skin.
Thanks to that, I got you."
Hosoda's skin★
Then Hosoda is...
I felt dizzy.
As I swayed, the thing caught me in its arms.
"Those who have the gift, yet cannot use it.
Those who cannot even drive out spirits, yet are more curious about them than anyone... We just love humans like that."
I was fading.
What on earth is happening to me?{p}As I slowly crumpled, its last words reached my ears.
"As the very finest food..."{p}

"Let's just go back."
When I said that, Hosoda nodded, looking relieved.
"Yeah.
Yeah, you're right."
He eagerly started to head back.
But then.{p}

There was nothing in front of us.
The hallway floorboards ended right at our feet.
Before us spread a darkness like outer space.
"This is... th-this is a hallucination, right?"
Hosoda took a step forward.
But there was no such thing as an 'invisible floor.'
"Waaah!"
I yanked Hosoda back as he lost his footing.{p}

The momentum sent both of us tumbling over.
"No way... is there really no way back?"
Hosoda's voice was tearful.
But there was nothing I could do.
I felt like crying myself.
Now there was only one way left for us to go.
I steeled myself and opened my mouth.{p}

We'd come this far; surely that was enough.
That's what I thought.
I quietly backed away.
But just then.{p}

Knock... knock... knock...
The sound of knocking echoed.
It wasn't me.
It wasn't Hosoda, or anyone else, either.
Anyone else...?
With a start, I looked at the door.{p}

Knock... knock... knock...
The knocking was coming from the other side of the door!
No doubt about it.
There's something in there.
"L-Let's just go home!"{p}

I was supposed to knock three times, right?
Just as I'd been told, I tried knocking three times.
Knock... knock... knock...
An answer...?
Knock... knock... knock...
An answer came back.
No doubt about it.
There's something in there!
"Stop it!
That's enough!
Let's go home, {a}!"
Hosoda's face was deathly pale.{p}

Just then, I was suddenly yanked upward with tremendous force.
"Waaaaaaaah!"
As if up and down had been flipped, I was slammed against the ceiling.
My arms and legs wouldn't move the way I wanted.{p}

I called out desperately to Hosoda, who was looking up at me.
"Help me!
Please, help...!"
But Hosoda shook his head.
"No. I won't."
I couldn't believe my ears.{p}

"Well, you turned me down when I asked you to be my friend, didn't you?
And on top of that, when I asked you a favor, you even made that put-upon face."
Hosoda seemed to be enjoying this, somehow.
"Th-That's not true!"
"You see, I never forget being hurt. Not as long as I live.
I didn't expect things to turn out like this, but now maybe you'll understand the pain in my heart."
Through my back, I felt the ceiling undulate.
It twisted a little, and a split opened up like a huge mouth.
I didn't need to look to know.
That mouth was slowly opening wide.
"I understand!
I'm sorry, it was my fault.
Please forgive me!"
I was drenched in sweat from head to toe.
Hosoda smiled at me, sweating as I was.
"Not a chance."{p}

Behind me, the split gaped wide open.
The giant mouth in the ceiling swallowed me whole.{p}
In the very last instant, I saw Hosoda walking out of the restroom.{p}

There was no way I could save him.
Even if I reached up, I couldn't reach the ceiling.
There was nothing at all I could do.
I'll just run.
I started to leave the restroom.
"{a}★"
I heard Hosoda's anguished cry.
"I'm sorry!"
Shouting that, I tried to dash out.
But my legs wouldn't move.
Not only that.{p}

"Whoa★"
Suddenly my body floated up into the air.{p}

I was slammed up right next to Hosoda.
The impact squeezed the air out of my lungs.
I choked in spite of myself.
As I coughed, someone grabbed my shoulder.{p}

"How could you, {a}!"
Hosoda's eyebrows were raised in fury as he glared at me.
"You were going to abandon me and go home!"
It was a frightening face, like nothing I'd ever seen on him.
He might hit me.
But just then, Hosoda's gaze shifted past me, to something behind me.
His face twisted in terror.
"Ah... ah... ah..."
As if he'd forgotten how to speak, Hosoda just kept moaning.{p}
I followed his gaze and turned around.{p}

The door of the second stall from the back stood open, and a masked girl was standing in it.
Suddenly, her voice echoed directly inside my head.
"You, or that one... which shall I choose?"
Her eyes were looking straight at me.
Me, and that one...?
Did she mean Hosoda?
"Which shall I choose?"
The voice echoed again.
She seemed to be thinking it over, but it also felt as if she was asking me.{p}Should I say something?
Tell her to choose him
Tell her to choose me

I hurriedly opened my mouth.
"Choose that one! Choose Hosoda!"
"{a}★
How could you..."
Hosoda's body came away from the ceiling.{p}

He hit the floor with a heavy thud.
"Ugh!"
The girl stood beside the groaning Hosoda.
She held out a slender hand.
"Get up."
Again, the voice echoed in my head.
But this time it seemed to be meant for Hosoda, not me.
Hosoda took her hand and stood up.
The eyes beneath the mask smiled.
"Just as that one said, I shall take you as my consort."
Consort?
Before I could think about what the word meant, the girl looked up at me again.
"The one left over is my gift to you.
Do with that one as you please."
Hearing that, Hosoda's face lit up.{p}

He looked up at me and smirked.
"So that's how it is."
I stared at him, wide-eyed.
I forced myself to swallow.
"H-Hosoda...?"
"{a}, you've abandoned me twice now, haven't you?
Even I have my limits, you know."
Hosoda was brimming with confidence, like a different person from a moment ago.
He must have been sure he wasn't going to be the one killed.
Did he mean to make his home in this old school building restroom, with the masked girl?
Hosoda nodded with a smile.
"You'll pay for betraying me with your life."{p}
The moment he said it, blood spurted from my neck.{p}

I hurriedly opened my mouth.
"I don't know what you're planning, but just choose me★"
Earlier, in a moment of weakness, I'd nearly abandoned Hosoda.
Hosoda called me his friend. I couldn't betray him any more than I already had.
Hosoda trembled.
"{a}.
You really are..."
Then he looked at the girl.
"No, take me!
{a} is my friend."
He said it firmly.
I felt the girl smile beneath her mask.
"Then both of you, is it?"
The instant I heard that, the ceiling lurched.
Its surface turned soft, and our bodies were sucked into it.
It was just like falling into water.
Hosoda flailed his arms and legs.{p}

"No!
I take it back, stop!
Just take {a} alone☆"
He was wailing pathetically.
"So this is all your friendship amounts to?"
The girl's voice spoke, and the ceiling turned springy again.
But Hosoda alone kept sinking, deeper and deeper.{p}

"No! I don't want this!
Help me!
Waaaaaaaaaah!"{p}

The ceiling swallowed his struggling hands and rippled for an instant with a soft slosh.
After that, there was no sign of Hosoda at all.{p}

The masked girl chuckled deep in her throat.
"By now you have learned how vile humans are.
Why not cut ties with such filthy things for good...?"
Behind the slits of her mask, her eyes gave off a sticky gleam.
But it didn't feel unpleasant at all...
Before I knew it, I was holding out my hand.
"I'll go.......... with you."
Her cold fingers closed around my hand.
I'd had enough of this grimy, filthy world.{p}I will live here.
In an eternity of time, set solid like jelly.{p}

"I can't abandon my family.
I'm sorry, Hosoda."
That was all I could say.
I do feel bad for Hosoda.
But even so, I didn't have the nerve to cut off my own family.
Hosoda had gone deathly pale.
It seemed he couldn't even speak anymore.{p}

When I came to, I was standing on the same restroom floor as before.
Hosoda was standing beside me too, looking dazed.
"I no longer need that one's life, nor your family's.
For I have obtained something just as precious."{p}
As I stood there dumbfounded, my neck was suddenly squeezed tight.{p}

"Ho... so... da...?"
It was Hosoda, his face twisted like a demon's.
"How dare you abandon me.
And I thought you were my friend."
He squeezed without mercy, and my consciousness began to fade.
I tried to tear his hands away, but I had no strength left.
Slowly sinking into the abyss of death, I finally understood the masked girl's words.
The thing she'd obtained, as precious as a life...{p}It was Hosoda's sanity, and the trust between us.{p}
